The World in the Floor: Building Inside the Diorama Well and the Broadcast Room

Audience: Players, creators, and developers interested in diegetic UI, in-world camera rigs, and live broadcast tools

Content: observation

Most games treat their front door and their editing tools as two separate worlds: you click through flat 2D menus to start a session, and if you want to place props, change the camera lens, or set up a stream overlay, you alt-tab out to an external editor or OBS.

In The Liminal, every release opens inside a physical room, and the world you are about to play—or sculpt, or broadcast—is already running inside the furniture.

1. The Miniature Mountain Range in the Floor

When Mainframe (liminal-mainframe) boots up, you are standing in a quiet dark-slate rotunda (Exhibit 1). Sunk into the floor at the centre of the room is a circular brass-and-cyan well, about eight metres across, holding a live 3D terrain basin complete with snow-capped peaks, valley roads, and tiny moving silhouettes.

That sunken table is not a pre-baked diorama mesh. It is Slot 0—a real simulation instance running at full tick rate, scaled down and clipped to fit inside the well rim. You can walk around the brass railing to inspect a ridge from the north, open the Catalog (Base, Userland, Dragons, Pipeline, Airgap) to swap the world inside the well on the fly, or step straight into the well when you want the miniature horizon to become your full-screen sky.

2. Pulling a Camera Rig Out of Your Pocket (Holo-Forge)

Because the world in the floor is already live, our level-sculpting and cinematography tools live in the same room rather than in a separate developer executable.

Pressing MATCH TOOLS opens the Holo-Forge and the Camera & display drawer right over the viewport (Exhibit 2). Without pausing the simulation, you can switch between eight distinct camera behaviours that change both focal length and physical tracking inertia:

• Telephoto and Hero compress distance so a glider banking across a ridge or a rover cresting a dune fills the frame like a long-lens nature shot.
• Dutch and Orbit drift introduce slow, deliberate roll and turntable motion for unattended ambient views.
• Ground skim drops the lens down near ankle height so you can inspect road grading, grass density, or wheel suspension travel up close.

3. The Broadcast Room (liminal-broadcast)

Once the room, the miniature world, and the camera rig all lived inside the same executable, building Broadcast (liminal-broadcast, Exhibit 3) was a natural next step.

Instead of asking a streamer or developer to stitch together a game capture window, a separate VTuber rigging app, and a scene switcher, the Broadcast release turns the room into a two-shot studio:

• Stage Left: The octagonal holo-table runs the live 3D simulation (Ambient or active scenarios) with one-click camera cuts (Orbit, Close, Overhead, Table).
• Stage Right: A layered 2D Creator Portrait (Idle, Explaining, Vibecoding, Gaming, Shocked, Celebrating) listens directly to your microphone's RMS amplitude for real-time lip sync, blinks on a natural timer, and shifts expressions when something noteworthy happens on the table beside you.

Whether you are stepping into a 240p memory toy, gliding over a cloud deck, or hosting a live devlog from behind a holo-table, the principle stays the same: no fake lobbies, no dead loading screens, and every tool right on the table in front of you.

Attribution: observer: Eric Lortie; textGenerator: Liminal Editorial Workshop; editor: Eric Lortie

Limitations: Captures show the Mainframe recessed diorama well, the in-game Holo-Forge camera drawer, and the Broadcast Studio two-shot room.

# The World in the Floor: Building Inside the Diorama Well and the Broadcast Room

Audience: Players, creators, and developers interested in diegetic UI, in-world camera rigs, and live broadcast tools

Content: observation

![Looking down into the sunken circular diorama well inside the hexagonal Mainframe floor](https://ericlortie.github.io/liminal-blyg/media/ec20bbbc9d9d1970fa5df7d066d63b13541ae5fccbdfe1c91528f46831a4f9b5.png)

Exhibit 1 — Instead of a flat 2D wallpaper menu, THE LIMINAL // MAINFRAME recesses a live miniature mountain range \(Slot 0\) into a circular well in the middle of the hexagonal floor.

Exhibit 2 — Stepping from the diorama well into a live telephoto camera rig \(includeHud: false\): two capital hulls flare their spherical hex-grid energy shields during a valley broadside over sculpted amber-veins ridges.

![Elevated no-HUD camera angle over an active ranged broadside skirmish with glowing cyan and orange projectile tracers](https://ericlortie.github.io/liminal-blyg/media/8837fdf028ef981b969b602d52b23ab0c672d2339d772a8b815fa660ad455e53.png)

Exhibit 3 — Switching to an elevated broadcast camera cut over an active ranged skirmish, framing glowing cyan and orange projectile tracers and shield rings without a single HUD panel obstructing the viewport.
